title: Tenant escalation: streaming stalls leading to cascading 5xxs and coordinated retry mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A strategic hotfix is required to stop tenant-specific streaming stalls from triggering cascading 5xx errors during customer escalations. Impact: multiple enterprise tenants observed ~10-30% request error amplification and long tail streaming timeouts during tenant surge windows. Root-cause hypothesis: a combination of (1) edge-proxy TCP keepalive churn under sustained multi-connection streaming, (2) runtime inflight KV cache compaction stalls that block async write paths, and (3) indiscriminate client retries causing request multiplication across proxy and runtime. This ticket implements a short-term mitigation and a staged production rollout plan, plus follow-up engineering work to permanently remove the blocking condition. Goals: stop immediate customer-facing 5xx waves, provide a transparent customer bridge with targeted routing, and instrument telemetry to validate behavior under load.
investigation_notes: Observed spike pattern: streaming requests show P99 latency rising from 1.2s to 12s coincident with tenant burst windows; 5xx rate jumps correspond to connection resets from front-door proxies.
Correlated host metrics: worker thread stalls (+40% blocked syscalls), elevated GC pause hints on older Java-hosted proxy process, and KV cache compaction spikes on GPU-hosted runtime nodes.
Client behavior: SDK retry settings (default exponential backoff) are amplifying load during the stall window; several customers were using aggressive retry wrappers.

Repro: internal replay harness reproduces the stall at ~70 RPS with streaming sessions >30s when mixed with KV cache compaction workload; disabling client retries prevents amplification but leaves initial timeouts.
Tentative root cause: proxy keepalive churn combined with synchronous KV compaction path that blocks the completion queue, producing connection resets which trigger client-led retry storms.
Evidence artifacts: tracing spans (trace IDs: feed: 0a1b2c3d), flamegraphs uploaded to runbook dashboard, and a curated sample from customer X shared in the incident doc.
proposed_mitigation: 1) Emergency hotfix (short-term, two-day) to add a per-tenant retry-holdback at front-door: incoming repeated requests within a 1s fingerprint window will be deduplicated and queued into a per-tenant deferred retry queue (leaky-bucket). 2) Introduce a streaming keepalive stabilization patch on proxy (increase keepalive threshold + graceful drain on connection reset). 3) Add a non-blocking KV compaction mode flag that offloads compaction to a background worker pool to break synchronous stalls. 4) Customer bridge: route impacted tenants to an alternative warm pool (dedicated capacity slice) while rolling fix. 5) SDK advisory: recommend backoff increase to customers under escalation.
implementation_plan: Phase A (hotfix): implement retry-holdback gate in edge proxy (fast path) + expose feature flag 'tenant_retry_holdback' on runtime config. Estimated 2 engineer-days.
Phase B (stabilize): backport keepalive tweaks to front-door proxy and enable non-blocking compaction flag in canary; measure P50/P90/P99 latency and 5xx rate. Estimated 3 engineer-days.
Phase C (canary + rollout): canary to 5% of traffic for 24h, 25% for 6h, then 100% if no regression. Use feature flags to rollback quickly.
Phase D (permanent): design work to remove synchronous compaction path and refactor KV eviction to non-blocking async flush (follow-up epic).
telemetry_and_sla_checks: Dashboards to watch: per-tenant inflight streams, per-tenant 5xx rate, proxy connection resets/sec, runtime KV compaction worker queue depth, P50/P90/P99 token latencies.
Safety gates for rollout: 30% drop in tenant 5xx rates (primary), no >5% increase in P99 latency for non-impacted tenants, and no sustained memory growth on proxy nodes.
Alert tripping thresholds: tenant 5xx increase >3x baseline for 10m, proxy resets >50/min on a node, KV compaction queue depth increase >2000 items.
Telemetry owners: Derek Zhang (SRE) for infra metrics, Priya Nair (Observability) for tracing and dashboards.
test_plan: Unit tests for retry-holdback fingerprint generation and queue semantics.
Integration: replay harness with mixed streaming + compaction workload to validate deduping prevents amplification.
Load test: 100 RPS sustained with concurrent streaming sessions to ensure no regression in throughput.
Chaos test: simulate proxy connection resets during canary to validate graceful drain and routing fallback.
deployment_and_rollout_notes: Feature flag 'tenant_retry_holdback' default OFF; enable for impacted tenant IDs first.
Canary on dedicated warm pool: route two enterprise tenants used in reproduction experiments (XCorp, FinSoft) before 5% global traffic.
Communication: PM to prepare status note for impacted customers before canary, SRE to monitor and be on-call during rollout window.
Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and shift tenant routing back to original pool; pre-built rollback script stored in runbook link.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Dedup window too long may delay legitimate retries and increase tail latency for clients that genuinely need retries.
Holdback queue introduces per-tenant memory pressure; mitigated by bounding queue size and rejecting requests with 429 when full.
Quickly enabling non-blocking compaction could mask underlying correctness bugs; will run extended test harness and data validation checks.
Routing tenants to warm pool increases cost temporarily but avoids widespread customer impact.
followups: ENG-923457 (placeholder): refactor KV compaction to async worker pool and add compaction instrumentation.
PM-4812: customer communication template and SLA credit evaluation for impacted enterprise customers.
DOC-237: SDK retry guidance update and code examples for exponential backoff best practices.
Security review: ensure retry-holdback fingerprinting doesn't leak PII; coordinate with Security for sign-off.
